name: Ferrari 125 F1
description:
125 F1, 1949 specification: 60° V12, 55 * 52.5mm = 1497cc, single overhead camshaft per bank, two-stage Roots supercharger, 280 bhp @ 7500 rpm (230 bhp in 1948 on a single blower)

Design: Gioachino Colombo, then Aurelio Lampredi
Transmission: 5 speed gearbox
Chassis: Tubular frame
Suspension: Front: double wishbones, transverse leaf spring Rear: swing axle, torsion bars
Dimensions: Wheelbase: 2320mm (1949, lengthened from 2160mm), weight: 710 kg
Top speed: 260 km/h
Years: 1948-1950

Ferrari's first Grand Prix car, and the first thing Enzo Ferrari built that was entirely his own. Colombo drew a supercharged 1.5 litre V12 to the same formula as the Alfa 158 he had drawn ten years earlier, and in 1949 - the one season Alfa Corse stayed at home - it finally got to win. Ascari took the Swiss and Italian Grands Prix, Villoresi took Zandvoort, and Ferrari has not missed a Grand Prix season since.

Note: this car is a rebuild on the Assetto Corsa Bootlegs Ferrari 500 F2 body. The physics are the 125 F1's; the shape is three years too late.
author: Assetto Corsa Bootlegs
